children: Tim Cook closed out his last day as chief executive officer of Apple on Monday, and his 15 years at the helm will go down as one of the most successful runs for a leader of a major consumer tech company.
His successor, John Ternus, will have big shoes to fill. Apple's senior vice president of hardware engineering takes over the CEO role on Tuesday.

But before the changing of the guard, Cook had one final message to share. "Sending lots of love to the Apple community on my last day as CEO," he wrote on X. "Thank you for being a constant source of inspiration."

From Aug. 23, 2011-one day before Cook became CEO-to the market close on Friday, Apple stock soared 2,296%, compared to the 563% rise of the S&P 500 in the same period, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That means an investment of $1,000 in Apple when Cook became CEO would now be worth $23,960, not including dividends.
Apple added $4.32 trillion in market capitalization under Cook, making it currently the second largest company in the world, behind only chip darling Nvidia.

The impressive stock gains were supported by the company's massive growth during Cook's time as CEO. On a last-12-month basis, Apple's sales were $467 billion as of the latest quarter, a 364% increase since the end of Steve Jobs's time as CEO.

"Cook's strength was execution, turning an already iconic company into one of the most profitable and valuable businesses the world has ever seen. For shareholders, it was one heck of a ride," Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, wrote on Monday.

Cook focused heavily on turning Apple into a successful services business-encompassing Apple Music, the App Store, and Apple TV-that has brought in billions of dollars of recurring revenue from people's existing devices. Cook also found a way to turn Apple into an incredibly sticky ecosystem by ensuring its devices and services interact seamlessly with each other, incentivizing customers who start with one Apple product to go on to buy multiple Apple products.

Ternus will now have to take what Cook helped build and expand on it with artificial intelligence at the core. Apple has already introduced AI updates, but customers and investors alike are waiting for more. Wall Street is highly anticipating the launch of an AI-powered Siri, which is set to come in September. The month will also bring the next iPhone launch, on the 9th, at which Apple is expected to unveil its first-ever foldable smartphone.

Ternus has a long-standing history with the company that gives some shareholders confidence that he is up for the challenge. He helped oversea the hardware engineering of several important products for Apple, including the iPad, AirPods, and Apple Watch. These launches, along with Cook's strategy of having Apple products interact with one another, have helped the business's growth soar.

"At 50, Ternus is roughly the same age Cook was when he replaced Jobs, but his engineering and product background offers Apple something different as it searches for its next big innovation and plays catch-up in AI," Woods wrote. "Cook proved you could successfully replace a legend, now Ternus gets the unenviable task."
The stage is set for Ternus to pick up where Cook left off-and the pressure is on for him to deliver.
